title: NCERT Figure 1.16 - the convention for an area element: the vector delta-S is its area delta-S times the unit normal n-hat drawn out of the plane.
unreadable: the lower half of the figure: an arbitrary closed surface drawn as a freeform blob with a small patch delta-S raised on it and a leader arrow pointing at the patch. There is no path or curve primitive here, so the blob is not attempted
the cyan gradient fill of both the area element and the blob, which is shading and carries nothing

NCERT sets the VECTOR delta-S and the unit vector n-hat in bold and the scalar area delta-S in plain italic; the renderer has no bold weight, so the equation delta-S = delta-S n-hat loses the one distinction it is printed to make
note: The area element is a TRUE parallelogram, built from one corner A = (20,150) and two edge vectors (210,0) and (60,110), so both pairs of opposite sides are equal by construction and the dot sits at the diagonals' common midpoint - (A+C)/2 and (B+D)/2 agree only if it really is a parallelogram. The normal is drawn at 72 degrees over a length of 130 and its tip is computed from those two numbers; no angle is CLAIMED for it, because the figure draws a 3-D normal in projection and the angle it makes on the page is an artefact of the viewpoint, not a quantity NCERT labels. NCERT prints the caption FIGURE 1.16 beneath; following the pilot's convention the redraw carries the drawing only.
